coverage: Curated original Fable recipes, not a mirror of the upstream library. All ten article use cases are mapped once; twelve additional library themes and three Fable-native implementation/completion workflows are included.

sources.scope: Public catalog themes; full prompt bodies were not imported.
Ten use cases, numbered by appearance in the article.
Original evidence, authority, and scaffold-completion workflows.

recipes.title: Challenge the changed behavior
inputs: Exact base and head refs
Diff, affected callers, and intended behavior
steps: Read repository instructions and compare the actual base/head; do not review an old pasted diff as current.
Construct counterexamples around each changed invariant, including failures and retries; trace callers outside the diff.
Try to refute each candidate before retaining it. Distinguish an observed failure from a static concern.
outputs: Ranked verified findings with file/line and ref evidence
recipes.gate: A clean diff review is not proof that the whole repository or production is healthy.

recipes.title: Protect existing consumers
inputs: Base/head refs
Public contracts and representative consumers
steps: Inventory exported names, serialized values, error shapes, defaults, and stored records affected by the change.
Compare old and new behavior from the consumer's perspective, including absent optional fields and older clients.
Design a compatibility probe and identify the migration or deprecation boundary; do not silently broaden the API.
recipes.gate: Unknown downstream usage remains unknown; a local caller search cannot prove external compatibility.

recipes.title: Validate scanner candidates
inputs: Sanitized findings and scanner version
Exact scanned ref and dependency lockfiles
steps: Separate duplicates and stale findings without discarding their evidence or scanner identifiers.
Trace reachable inputs, privileges, deployment assumptions, and affected versions; do not assume most findings are false positives.
Record a safe local verification plan and prioritize remediation by supported impact and exposure.
outputs: Finding disposition ledger with confidence and supporting evidence
recipes.gate: Never dismiss or suppress a finding solely because the model could not reproduce it.

recipes.title: Trace hostile input to authority
inputs: In-scope entry points and trust boundaries
Authorization policy and sanitized test fixtures
steps: Map untrusted sources to sensitive sinks and identify which principal authorizes each transition.
Check alternate encodings, redirects, retries, cross-tenant identifiers, and denied paths where relevant to the target.
Challenge candidate bypasses using isolated fixtures; report the tested boundary rather than a blanket secure verdict.
recipes.gate: No production exploitation, credential reads, wallet activity, or external probes are authorized by this recipe.

recipes.title: Draft only what actually shipped
inputs: Explicit release base/head or tags
Merged PR evidence and release/deployment status
steps: Resolve the release range and verify inclusion from commits; do not treat every recently merged PR as included.
Describe user-visible changes and required actions, separating reverted, disabled, unreleased, and deployed work.
Cross-check each claim against code and observed validation, and mark missing deployment evidence.
outputs: Draft release notes with traceable change references
recipes.gate: Drafting notes does not authorize tags, publication, merging, or deployment.

recipes.title: Reconcile promises with implementation
inputs: Changed refs and affected behavior
Documentation surfaces and edit authorization
steps: Find public and machine-facing promises affected by the diff, including examples, help output, and generated references.
Build a must-update/preserve/generated/unknown hit list before editing; follow the source generator where one exists.
Update only the authorized surfaces and exercise changed examples when safe; retain qualifications for untested environments.
recipes.gate: Do not turn planned, preview-only, or unverified behavior into a live capability claim.

recipes.title: Turn a goal into finishable changes
inputs: User outcome and non-goals
Existing implementation, issues, and constraints
steps: Inspect what exists before proposing new components or issues; identify the smallest end-to-end outcome.
Order bounded slices by dependency and assign an observable acceptance check to each one.
Separate evidence-backed work from discovery spikes, owner decisions, and optional improvements.
outputs: Acceptance evidence and decision blockers per slice
recipes.gate: Issue drafts are not permission to create issues; estimates are assumptions, not delivery promises.

recipes.title: Make a test capable of catching the bug
inputs: Behavior contract and target ref
Existing test runner and authorized edit scope
steps: Derive assertions from intended behavior, not from the implementation's current output.
Add deterministic boundary and denial cases using existing helpers; avoid mocks that bypass the behavior under test.
Where feasible demonstrate failure before the fix and success after it, then run the affected suite.
outputs: Actual commands, outcomes, and pre-fix evidence or limitation
recipes.gate: Do not weaken assertions, skip a failing check, or change expected behavior merely to obtain green tests.

recipes.title: Find missing behavioral proof
inputs: Changed behavior and existing tests
Coverage report with ref and command, when available
steps: Map requirements to actual assertions and distinguish execution coverage from meaningful behavioral proof.
Inspect untested denial, cancellation, recovery, migration, and integration paths relevant to the target.
Rank additions by failure impact and show which present tests would stay green if the behavior broke.
recipes.gate: Never invent a coverage percentage or imply that line coverage proves correctness.

recipes.title: Separate CI regressions from runner failures
inputs: Run/job identifiers and exact failed SHA
Sanitized logs, workflow, and last passing comparison
steps: Find the earliest causal failure and compare inputs, runtime, permissions, and code with the last passing run.
Keep hypotheses for code, test, environment, and infrastructure separate; select the smallest discriminating check.
Propose a minimal fix with a same-SHA rerun plan and a regression check for the actual cause.
outputs: Minimal repair plan and exact rerun target
recipes.gate: A green run on another SHA does not validate this head; never remove a required gate to make CI pass.

recipes.title: Build the minimum useful repository map
inputs: Question, scope, and current ref
Repository instructions and entry points
steps: Read governing instructions, then trace only the entry points, owners, callers, and tests needed for the question.
Separate executable implementation from examples, dead paths, generated artifacts, and aspirational documentation.
Produce a compact evidence map with the next file or experiment needed to resolve each consequential unknown.
recipes.gate: Do not load unrelated repository or conversation history merely because it is available.

recipes.title: Compare the smallest viable designs
inputs: Decision and success criteria
Current architecture and non-negotiable constraints
steps: Include extending the current design and doing nothing among the options when viable.
Compare integration cost, failure modes, reversibility, ownership, and validation needs using repository evidence.
Recommend one bounded experiment and state what result would change the recommendation.
recipes.gate: Do not invent benchmark results or adopt a new framework just to justify a preferred design.

recipes.title: Turn a symptom into a falsifiable case
inputs: Expected and observed behavior
Sanitized reproducer and exact environment/ref
steps: Write competing causal explanations and record what evidence would distinguish them.
Reduce the case without deleting the trigger; identify the first violated invariant rather than the final error message.
Prepare an isolated regression test specification and keep unreproduced hypotheses explicitly tentative.
recipes.gate: Do not claim a root cause from a plausible explanation alone.

recipes.title: Make timing failures repeatable
inputs: Concurrent paths and shared state
Ordering guarantees and retry policy
steps: Draw the read/write and ownership sequence, including cancellation and duplicate delivery.
Identify a violating interleaving and design controllable barriers or fake-clock fixtures instead of sleep-based luck.
Check whether the proposed invariant survives retries and partial failures, not just the happy schedule.
recipes.gate: One successful stress run does not prove race freedom.

recipes.title: Measure before changing the hot path
inputs: Representative workload and performance objective
Profiles with environment and ref metadata
steps: Separate measured bottlenecks from intuition and identify the cost center and workload assumptions.
Design a matched baseline/candidate measurement with correctness and resource guardrails.
Report distributions and experimental limitations; reject gains that merely shift work or disable checks.
recipes.gate: No speedup claim without comparable observed measurements.

recipes.title: Bound an upgrade's blast radius
inputs: Current lockfile and intended version
Official change notes and relevant integration paths
steps: Resolve versions and verify current primary documentation before interpreting compatibility or advisories.
Map changed APIs, transitive impacts, platform support, and permission or licensing questions.
Choose a bounded upgrade slice with smoke tests, fallback, and a decision list for unresolved risks.
recipes.gate: Do not equate a successful install with runtime compatibility or legal approval.

recipes.title: Plan a reversible data transition
inputs: Old/new schema and deployed reader/writer versions
Data constraints, volume assumptions, and recovery requirements
steps: Map mixed-version operation and expand/backfill/contract boundaries before touching stored data.
Specify idempotent progress, interruption recovery, compatibility probes, and a realistic restoration path.
Distinguish reversible code changes from irreversible data effects and reserve the latter for owner approval.
recipes.gate: No live migration, data deletion, or backup claim without separate authorization and evidence.

recipes.title: Simplify without erasing compatibility
inputs: Behavior to preserve and allowed scope
Callers, serialized references, and characterization tests
steps: Build the complete scoped hit list and classify compatibility-preserved, generated, and uncertain references.
Prefer small behavior-preserving edits; do not combine unrelated cleanup with the requested change.
Run characterization and consumer checks, and explain every intentional retained old name or path.
recipes.gate: No destructive cleanup based solely on a text search finding zero callers.

recipes.title: Test the seams, not only the helpers
inputs: Component boundaries and public invocation path
Isolated fixtures and allowed test commands
steps: Exercise the actual public entry point through relevant serialization, authorization, and state transitions.
Add failure, timeout, cancellation, duplicate, and resume cases where applicable without bypassing the seam with mocks.
Verify the final receipt or externally observable result contains the complete journey, not only the last step.
outputs: Observed state/receipt assertions and untested dependencies
recipes.gate: Mocks and dry runs must not be reported as live integration validation.

recipes.title: Find the queue that blocks completion
inputs: Repository scope and explicit time window
Accessible PR, issue, review, and CI records with coverage limits
steps: Retrieve the actual records and separate waiting for review, failed checks, decisions, dependencies, and abandoned work.
Use consistent windows and denominators; report missing repositories, pagination, and incomplete periods.
Recommend the smallest intervention tied to a named blocker; measure completion and rework rather than raw code volume.
outputs: Prioritized unblock actions and measurement caveats
recipes.gate: No fabricated telemetry, causal AI-productivity claim, or developer ranking from activity counts.

recipes.title: Delegate independent questions, not authority
inputs: Task map, active runtime capability, and ECF contract
Current worker limits and authority boundaries
steps: Delegate only disjoint questions that benefit from independent evidence; keep routine changes single-agent.
Respect the active model/profile and thread/depth limits; do not change runtime configuration to satisfy the prompt.
Give each worker a bounded evidence output and stop rule; the coordinator challenges results and owns integration.
outputs: Actual delegation trace or honest single-agent fallback
recipes.gate: Never invent worker IDs, independence, model settings, or runtime-enforced guarantees.

recipes.title: Complete an existing vertical slice
inputs: User-visible acceptance outcome and authorized scope
Existing scaffold, related issues/PRs, and current refs
steps: Prove what already works and locate the missing path from public entry point to final observable result.
Complete the smallest authorized slice using existing modules; do not create a parallel subsystem or hide missing work behind a new stub.
Validate entry-point reachability, denial/recovery behavior, and receipts, then document only proven capability.
outputs: Completed bounded implementation or exact blocker
End-to-end acceptance evidence and remaining scaffold map
recipes.gate: A new file, exported helper, or passing mocked test does not establish a usable feature.

recipes.title: Verify the interface in its real states
inputs: Target pages, supported viewports, and critical tasks
Browser evidence or an explicit browser-tool limitation
steps: Inspect loading, empty, error, denied, long-content, and success states across relevant viewport sizes.
Check focus order, keyboard operation, labels, touch targets, overlap, and component consistency with observed evidence.
Separate static HTML concerns from browser-confirmed defects and give a minimal reproduction for each finding.
outputs: Actionable UI findings with observation limits
recipes.gate: Do not claim visual, screen-reader, or accessibility certification from static source inspection alone.

recipes.title: Repair the proven cause, not the symptom
inputs: Verified failure or explicitly qualified hypothesis
Authorized edit scope and a discriminating regression check
steps: Capture the failing case before the patch where feasible, preserving unrelated changes and existing safety gates.
Make the smallest causal repair through the real invocation path, updating affected callers without unrelated cleanup.
Run the regression and affected checks at the final head; retain failed or unavailable checks as blockers.
outputs: Minimal repair diff with causal rationale
Failing-before/passing-after evidence or an explicit limitation
recipes.gate: Do not patch production state, suppress security findings, or weaken tests to manufacture a successful repair.

recipes.title: Reconcile done claims before handoff
inputs: Acceptance criteria and exact final head
Diff, command outputs, CI state, and prior claims
steps: Check every acceptance claim against the final ref and distinguish implemented, locally tested, CI-passed, merged, and deployed states.
Identify stale receipts, skipped jobs, unknown coverage, and owner-only decisions without smoothing them into success.
Provide the next concrete action and a compact ECF Workflow Trace; propose memory handoff only through an available authorized integration.
outputs: Honest completion status, blockers, and next action
recipes.gate: Never claim independent review, cross-platform success, merge, deployment, or persistent memory without evidence.
